schema.title: Response List Work Orders Api Work Orders Get

get.description:
Get work order detail with operations (program-scoped).

Build Spec §5.1 documents this endpoint as "Get work order detail
with operations" and §3.1 names ``operations: list[Operation]`` on
the WorkOrder entity.  The list endpoint continues to return the
lighter ``WorkOrderOut`` (no operations) so paginated responses
stay small; this detail endpoint hydrates the operations array so
the frontend WO detail page (UX spec §5.3) renders its Operations
tab without a follow-up fetch.

Ordering: operations are returned by ``sequence`` ascending, which
matches the UX spec's operations table display order and avoids
client-side re-sorting.

Emits `ETag: "<version>"` per UX spec v1.5.1 §6.3.1 so the
client can send it back as `If-Match` on a subsequent mutation
without re-reading the body.

patch.description:
Update work order fields (draft only, version check).

Accepts the version assertion via either body.version or
If-Match per UX spec §6.3.1; `resolve_version_assertion`
rejects mismatched / missing / weak-ETag cases.

post.description:
Release work order (draft → released).

SOD-004 (spec §4.2, §5.1): author cannot release same WO.
Enforcement happens in the service layer.  Accepts either
body.version or If-Match per §6.3.1.
Recall work order — If-Match + body.version per §6.3.1.

patch.description:
Fix Graph (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.4.6).

Apply predecessor edits + re-validate.  Engineer-only,
hold-state-only.  On validation failure the graph is NOT
mutated and the response is 422 with per-error detail;
on success the WO version bumps, has_graph_issue resets to
false, and the response returns the updated WO + its
operations with fresh predecessor sets.

Cross-program returns 404 (§3.2 existence-leak rule), inherited
from get_work_order inside the service.

post.description:
Report Graph Issue (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.4.6).

Runs the DAG validator on the WO's current predecessor graph
without applying any change.  Always 200 regardless of graph
state — `validation_errors` is empty on pass, populated on
fail.  When issues are found, server-side atomically sets
has_graph_issue=true and emits `work_order.graph_issue_reported`.

Put work order on hold (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.3).

`force_stop_labor` (default false) is the stop-work flag: when
true the server atomically stops every active labor entry on
child operations and emits a `labor.stopped_by_hold` audit event
per entry.  The response carries `stopped_labor_entries` so the
frontend can render the §5.3 stop-work banner and so the later
SSE `wo_state_changed` payload (§6.5.2) can reuse the same
data shape.
Resume work order from hold.
Mark work order complete (all ops must be complete).
Close work order (final QA closure).
Create operation on a draft work order.

get.description:
Enriched operation detail per UX spec v1.5.1 §5.4.8.

Emits `ETag: "<version>"` per §6.3.1 so the client can send it
back as `If-Match` on subsequent operation mutations.

Drives the engineer Operation Detail page (§5.4.11) and the SSE
reconnect contract (§6.5.2 — clients refetch this endpoint on every
reconnect as the authoritative state-reconciliation surface,
regardless of any best-effort SSE replay).

Authorization (§6.7.4 entity-detail GET exception): the X-Program-Id
middleware skips header membership comparison on this route; service-
layer enforcement against entity.program_id (via parent WO) returns
404 on cross-program per the §3.2 existence-leak rule.

patch.description:
Update operation (draft WO only, version check).

§6.3.1 concurrency: body.version OR If-Match — route resolves
via `resolve_version_assertion`.

delete.description: Delete operation (draft WO only, version check).

post.description: Reorder operations by sequence (draft WO only).

schema.title: Response Reorder Operations Api Work Orders  Wo Id  Operations Reorder Post

post.description: Start operation, create labor entry.  §6.3.1 version assertion.
Stop active labor entry for the current user.
Complete operation (rules checked).
Put operation on hold.
Create a labor entry on an operation.

patch.description:
Update a labor entry (own or any per permission).

Spec §5.3: labor:update_own allows updating own entries,
labor:update_any allows updating any entry.  §6.3.1 version
assertion via body.version OR If-Match.

get.description:
Subscribe to sub-second operation updates (UX spec v1.5.1 §6.5.2).

Events emitted: hold_point_changed, wo_state_changed,
labor_activity, operation_reopened (GC-2 reopen — fires when an
NCR disposition drives the op from complete → in_progress;
payload carries ncr_id, disposition, and the new
execution_cycle), ping (20s heartbeat), auth_expired (on token
expiry), buffer_reset (when `Last-Event-ID` replay is
unsatisfiable), error (on internal stream failure — client
falls back to 30s polling per §6.5.2 error mapping), done
(when the parent WO transitions to `closed` — the op stream is
permanently terminal at that point).

Authorization:
  - op:read permission at the route level.
  - service-layer scope check via get_operation (404 on cross-program
    per §3.2 / §6.7.4 entity-detail existence-leak rule).
  - the program-scope middleware exempts this path from header-based
    comparison for the same reason the plain entity-detail GET is
    exempt — the entity's program_id is the authority.

Reconnect contract: the client performs a mandatory REST refetch of
GET /api/operations/{op_id} on every reconnect (§6.5.2).  SSE
replay is best-effort only; on buffer miss the server emits
buffer_reset and the client leans on the refetch.

Last-Event-ID parsing is permissive — a malformed header falls
back to "no replay hint," which matches a first-connect.  The
alternative (400) would surface as an unfriendly reconnect loop
on the client without adding safety.

Paginated Inspection Queue (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.5.5).

Drives the inspector worklist and the qa_manager read-only drill-
through.  Rows carry server-derived `state`, `hold_point_status`,
`is_overdue`, and `overdue_since` — the frontend does not derive
any of these (§5.4.3 explicit prohibition).

Program scope: honors the X-Program-Id contract (§6.7) via the
caller's claim set passed through auth.programs.  Multi-program
`*` scope is accepted by this endpoint per §5.2 (Inspection Queue
is one of the enumerated list pages that support "All").

post.description: Record an inspection event (SOD-001 enforced in service).
Record a sign-off event (SOD-005 enforced in service).

patch.description:
Canonical PATCH for labor-entry corrections (UX spec §3.2).

§6.3.1 version assertion via body.version OR If-Match.

Engineer stops another user's active labor entry (UX §5.4.9).

§6.3.1 version assertion via `labor_entry_version` body field
OR `If-Match` header.

Operator requests an engineer stop another user's entry

§6.3.1 version assertion via `labor_entry_version` body field
OR `If-Match` header.

Operator flags a labor entry for engineer correction review
(UX §5.4.5).

No state transition — audit-only.  Returns 204 because the
resource state did not change from the caller's perspective;
the attention signal lives in the audit trail.  `response_class=
Response` + explicit empty 204 body is FastAPI's no-content
contract — a response_model + None body would fail the
is_body_allowed_for_status_code assert at import time.

Replace evidence_refs on an NCR (build spec v1.4.2 Decision 1).

Permissions: ncr:disposition OR ncr:close — either role is
authorized to attach completion evidence during the remediation
cycle.  Since a FastAPI dep cannot OR two permissions, the
check is inline here.  Any other NCR-edit surface stays off
this route; broader NCR edits are a separate slice.

Disposition an NCR (open → dispositioned).

SOD-002 (spec §4.2): the initiator cannot disposition the same NCR.
Enforcement happens in the service layer.

List material certifications (paginated, program-scoped).

UX spec v1.5.1 §5.7 Material Certification List: status filter
(quarantine / accepted / rejected / consumed / expired / scrapped)
and "All (assigned programs)" multi-program read per §6.7.1.
Parity patch closes the gap between Build Spec §5.6 (write routes
only) and the UX spec's requirement for a real list surface.

post.description: Receive a material lot into quarantine.

patch.description: Accept a quarantined lot (SOD-003 enforced in service).

get.description:
List parts (paginated, program-scoped).

UX spec v1.5.1 §3.2 routes ``/parts`` to a Part Instance List
surface and §6.7.1 includes Part List in the "All (assigned
programs)" multi-program read set.  Parity patch closes the gap
between Build Spec §5.7 (write-only + traceability) and the UX
spec's list requirement.

No server-side filters are added in this patch — spec §5.8 does
not enumerate filter controls for the part list and the service
stays minimal.  Clients that need client-side filters already
have enough data in PartOut.

schema.title: Response List Parts Api Parts Get

post.description: Create a serialized part instance in `raw` status.

patch.description:
Update a part (status/location/parent).  Transitions gated in service.

Scrap transitions also require `part:scrap`.  UX spec v1.5.1
§5.6.5 names qa_manager as the product-authorized scrap role;
the admin role additionally carries part:scrap as a Phase-1
break-glass lane (see ROLE_PERMISSIONS in forge.api.auth).  The
route's base dependency is `part:update` so legitimate non-scrap
edits from operator / engineer / qa_manager / admin all reach
the service; the service enforces the scrap-specific permission
itself when the requested status is `scrapped`.

get.description:
Get a single part by ID (program-scoped).

UX spec v1.5.1 §6.7.4 entity-detail authorization exception:
cross-program access returns **404, not 403** — surfacing 403 would
confirm the part exists in a program the caller cannot see.  The
shape is intentionally indistinguishable from "no such record."
``part_service.get_part`` enforces that contract directly (via
``_load_part_in_scope``).

Separate from ``/{part_id}/traceability``: the traceability
endpoint carries the full assembly + child chain which is more
expensive; the frontend part detail page wants to render the
part header first, then fetch traceability in parallel.
Return the full traceability chain for a part.

List documents (paginated).

Checklist 3B do-not-advance: GET endpoints require doc:read, NOT

Scope permissions (build spec v1.4.2 Decision 1):

Program is the X-Program-Id header's selected UUID; the
registry row will bind to that program at confirm-time so
cross-program reuse of the same s3_key is rejected.  Wildcard
scope is rejected upstream by require_program_id.

Confirm a presigned upload landed and promote the registry row.

Frozen spec surface: body is {s3_key, content_hash}.  Scope,
program, filename, content_type, and size_bytes are already on
the pending registry row written at upload-url time; the
confirm step reads them from there.  Live mode verifies the
SHA-256 against S3 GetObjectAttributes; stub mode trusts the
client attestation (no real object storage to compare
against).  Returns the canonical EvidenceRef shape the client
persists on its inspection / NCR write.

Dashboard summary for a single program (UX spec §5.1).

Program scope: `X-Program-Id` must resolve to a single UUID.
The middleware rejects `*` on this route (dashboard is not on

in depth.  The service resolves the UUID to the program's
`code` and scopes every aggregate to that one program.

Tile audience: UX §5.1 names Unresolved Conditional Findings
and Overdue Inspections as "QA manager dashboard additions."
Tiles are filtered by caller.roles in the service layer, not
hidden client-side — a UI bug cannot leak management-only
counts to operators or inspectors.

Returns 400 MISSING_PROGRAM_CONTEXT if the header is absent,

get.description:
System Health composite for the admin panel (UX §5.10).

Returns per-component health plus a rolled-up overall status.
Components that the backend cannot truthfully measure (ECS
task status in Phase 1) report `unknown` with an explanatory
message — the slice deliberately does not fabricate AWS
state.

No X-Program-Id required: the /api/admin/* namespace is
program-agnostic per UX spec v1.5.1 §6.7 (R5-R2-ISSUE-008),
and the middleware bypasses the header contract for the
entire prefix.

Paginated audit event list with filters (UX spec §6.6.2).

Current filters: entity_type, entity_id, actor_user_id, action,
timestamp_from/to.  The spec also names `program_id`; deferred
— see audit_service docstring for why.

Typed PaginatedResponse[AuditEventOut] gives the OpenAPI
generator the precise item shape so the generated client can
bind to the envelope + item type directly.
Single audit-event detail.

Audit-chain integrity summary (UX spec §6.6.2).

Runs the full hash-chain verifier on every call.  Acceptable at
current audit volumes; if it becomes a hot path the daily-job
result can be cached and surfaced here, with this endpoint
reserved for explicit admin "refresh" actions.

Return the authenticated caller's live DB profile.

Any authenticated user (no specific permission required per
spec §5.14).  Returns roles + program memberships + the derived
permission union so the UI does not need a second round-trip.

AdminHealthOut.title: AdminHealthOut
AdminHealthOut.description:
Admin System Health composite (UX spec §5.10 / build spec §7).

Top-level `status` is the worst status across the KNOWN
components — unknown components do not propagate into the
overall roll-up so the endpoint is not permanently yellow
while ECS instrumentation is still being planned.

Component layout mirrors the spec's four named legs plus the
`service` liveness signal already carried on /health:

  - service:          app process liveness + env/version echo
  - database:         RDS connectivity via `SELECT 1`
  - audit_chain:      hash-chain integrity (reuses verifier)
  - worm_replication: S3 replication lag vs. spec §7.2 SLA
  - ecs:              task status — currently `unknown`

`generated_at` is the server wall clock for the admin poll
interval (UX §5.10) — clients can render "updated Ns ago"
without holding their own clock.

AuditActor.title: AuditActor
AuditActor.description:
Actor attribution block per UX spec v1.5.1 §6.6.1.

`display_name` is server-resolved (joined from the users table)
so the frontend can render attribution without a per-row follow-up.
`role_at_time_of_event` is captured at audit-write time (column
`user_role` on AuditRecord) — historical role survives even after
the user's current role assignments change.

AuditEventOut.title: AuditEventOut
AuditEventOut.description:
Single audit-event read shape per UX spec v1.5.1 §6.6.1.

`audit_id` is the AuditRecord primary key (the spec name is
`audit_id`; the database column is `id`).  `integrity_hash`
surfaces the per-record SHA-256 from the hash-chain so the
frontend audit detail can render the chain anchor for an admin
investigating a verification failure.

AuditIntegrityOut.title: AuditIntegrityOut
AuditIntegrityOut.description:
Audit-chain integrity summary per UX spec v1.5.1 §6.6.2.

`status` is the high-level pass/fail flag the admin Audit
Integrity panel polls every five minutes (§6.6.3).  The `failures`
list is exposed in full so an admin investigating a chain break
can identify the exact record + field without a follow-up call.

`last_verified_at` is the wall-clock time of THIS verification
run (not a daemon-managed timestamp), so a manual poll always
reflects the most recent data the server can see.

CertStatus.title: CertStatus
CertStatus.description:
Material certification lifecycle (spec §3.1 MaterialCertification).

`scrapped` is a terminal verdict for stock that has been condemned
(lot failure discovered post-accept, in-process damage, or NCR-linked
disposal).  UX spec v1.5.1 §5.7 enumerates `scrapped` on the
materials filter vocabulary.

ChatRequest.title: ChatRequest
ChatRequest.description:
Request body for /api/chat and /api/chat/stream.

`parameters` lets structured callers pass IDs directly without
relying on keyword extraction from the query text.

ComponentOut.title: ComponentOut
ComponentOut.description:
One infrastructure component's health report.

`status` is the tri-state (plus unknown) indicator from the
spec's green/yellow/red language.  `summary` is a short
human-readable line the admin UI renders next to the color
dot.  `details` carries component-specific diagnostics for
the expanded view — always a dict (empty if nothing to show)
so the frontend can iterate without a null check.

CpmNodeOut.title: CpmNodeOut
CpmNodeOut.description:
Per-operation CPM output in working hours (relative to baseline_start).

slack = late_start - early_start.  Zero-slack operations lie on
the critical path.

query.title: Query
query.description: Filter params to pre-select on the target page

DashboardDrillThrough.title: DashboardDrillThrough
DashboardDrillThrough.description:
Where clicking a dashboard tile should take the user.

Paths are the canonical frontend routes from UX spec §3.2.  Query
params mirror the server-enforceable filter vocabulary (e.g. the
Inspection Queue accepts `state=overdue` and `state=conditional`
per §5.5.5).  Empty query dict means "no filter, just open the
target page."

Keeping query as a generic dict rather than a discriminated union
because each tile's destination has its own filter vocabulary —
typing every variant would balloon the schema for no frontend
benefit (the client just passes the dict through to its router).

program_scope.title: Program Scope
program_scope.description: Program codes aggregated over.  This endpoint is single-program only (the middleware rejects X-Program-Id: *), so the list always contains exactly one entry — the code of the program named by the active X-Program-Id header.  Carried as a list rather than a scalar so the shape does not break if a future slice opens dashboard to a bounded multi-program mode.

DashboardSummaryOut.title: DashboardSummaryOut
DashboardSummaryOut.description:
Top-level dashboard payload (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.1).

Structure:
  - `tiles` is the ordered list of count-cards (open NCRs,
    overdue inspections, unresolved conditional findings).  The
    ordering is the server's recommended display order; the
    frontend renders top-to-bottom as-is.
  - `work_order_status_counts` backs the "Build Status" card
    that the UX spec names explicitly but doesn't coerce into a
    single count — WO status is inherently multi-valued.
  - `program_scope` echoes the program codes the server
    aggregated over so the frontend can render
    "showing PROG-RS25" or "across 3 programs" without
    re-reading the X-Program-Id header (avoids echo drift if the
    header and the authorized scope ever disagree).
  - `generated_at` supports the 60-second polling interval
    (UX §5.1) — clients can display "updated Ns ago" without
    keeping their own wall clock.

visible_to_roles.title: Visible To Roles
visible_to_roles.description: Roles for which this tile is included in the response (UX spec §5.1 audience — server-enforced).

DashboardTileOut.title: DashboardTileOut
DashboardTileOut.description:
A single clickable card on the dashboard (UX spec §5.1).

Uniform row shape so the frontend iterates instead of branching.
`key` is the stable machine identifier (used for ordering, test
assertions, and a11y labels).  `label` is the user-facing string.
`value` is always an int for Phase 1 — every named tile is a
count — but declaring it as int here rather than using a union
keeps the OpenAPI contract simple; non-count tiles would get
their own schema variant.

`visible_to_roles` is informational on the wire — a tile only
appears in the response if the caller is authorized to see it
(the service filters the list).  It is included so a frontend
feature flag (or an admin-mode "preview as role X" tool) can
reason about audience without duplicating the mapping.

DeadLetterOut.title: DeadLetterOut
DeadLetterOut.description:
Dead-letter delivery projection for the admin UI (spec §5.13).

event_type and aggregate_* come from the DomainEvent row (resolved
by the service).  attempt_count / last_error / last_attempt_at
surface why the delivery ended up here so an operator can decide
whether to retry or escalate.

DocumentFinalize.title: DocumentFinalize
DocumentFinalize.description:
Request body for POST /api/documents/{id}/finalize.

content_hash is the SHA-256 (hex) of the uploaded content, computed
client-side.  Spec §3.1 requires 64 hex characters (SHA-256 length).

EvidenceConfirmRequest.title: EvidenceConfirmRequest
EvidenceConfirmRequest.description:
Request body for POST /api/evidence/confirm.

Frozen spec surface: {s3_key, content_hash}.  Scope, program,
filename, content_type, and size_bytes are all already bound
on the pending registry row written at upload-url time — the
server reads them from there, not the confirm body.

EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef
EvidenceRef.description:
Canonical structured evidence reference persisted on parents.

Built server-side from an EvidenceConfirmation row — the client
never writes these fields directly.  Returned verbatim on read
so the UI has the metadata it needs without a second query.

EvidenceScope.title: EvidenceScope
EvidenceScope.description:
EvidenceConfirmation attribution scope (build spec §5.8 Decision 1).

Distinguishes inspection evidence from NCR remediation evidence so
the parent-entity program check, scope cross-check, and cleanup
query all have a single source of truth for "what is this blob
attached to?".  Documents are not in this enum — they use the
ControlledDocumentRef path, not the structured evidence registry.

EvidenceUploadUrlResponse.title: EvidenceUploadUrlResponse
EvidenceUploadUrlResponse.description:
Response for POST /api/evidence/upload-url.

`upload_headers` are the exact headers the client must echo on
the PUT so S3 validates the SHA-256 checksum and content-type
server-side.  Returning them as a map lets the client's upload
library set them without knowing the AWS header-name
conventions.

FlagCorrectionIn.title: FlagCorrectionIn
FlagCorrectionIn.description:
Request body for POST /api/labor-entries/{id}/flag-correction.

No version field — flag-correction does not transition state,
it only emits an audit event for the engineer to notice on
their next poll of the Work Order view.  Adding a version
guard would add concurrent-edit failure modes with no
corresponding correctness benefit.

ForceStopIn.title: ForceStopIn
ForceStopIn.description:
Request body for POST /api/labor-entries/{id}/force-stop.

`rationale` floor of 10 chars tracks UX spec §5.4.9 verbatim —
short enough to catch accidental empty submits, long enough to
force a one-phrase explanation for the audit trail.  The spec
names `labor_entry_version` on the body; §6.3.1 also permits
an `If-Match` header, so the body field is now optional and
the route reconciles via `resolve_version_assertion`.

GraphPatchIn.title: GraphPatchIn
GraphPatchIn.description:
Request body for PATCH /api/work-orders/{id}/graph.

`version` is the WO's current version per §6.3 optimistic
locking.  A stale value returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT — same
posture as every other WO state-transition endpoint.
`predecessor_changes` is a batch: the server applies all
edits atomically and validates the resulting graph; a single
validation failure rolls back every edit in the batch.

GraphPatchOut.title: GraphPatchOut
GraphPatchOut.description:
Success response for PATCH /api/work-orders/{id}/graph.

Returns the updated work order entity plus every operation in
that WO with its current predecessor set.  Shipping the full
op list (not just changed ones) means the client does not
have to reconcile partial deltas against a stale local cache —
rehydration from this payload is one round trip.

GraphValidateOut.title: GraphValidateOut
GraphValidateOut.description:
Response for POST /api/work-orders/{id}/graph/validate.

Always 200.  `has_graph_issue` echoes the server's post-
validation state on the WO; the frontend keys the button
swap (Report Graph Issue → Fix Graph) off this field so the
contract has a single source of truth.  `validation_errors`
is the full list of failures (possibly empty).

GraphValidationErrorOut.title: GraphValidationErrorOut
GraphValidationErrorOut.description:
One validation error on the wire (UX spec §5.4.6).

`code` is spec-stable (WO-REL-101/102/103).  `detail` is a
human-readable sentence specific enough to name the offending
operation(s) — the spec shows examples like
"Cycle detected: Op 3 → Op 5 → Op 3".  `operation_ids` lets
the frontend highlight the involved nodes without re-running
any validation logic client-side.

HoldPointStatus.title: HoldPointStatus
HoldPointStatus.description:
Server-derived inspection hold-point status (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.4.3).

Computed from an operation's inspection_hold flag and the latest
InspectionResult in the current execution_cycle.  Surfaced on the
operation detail response so the frontend never has to traverse
inspection history client-side (spec §5.4.3 explicit prohibition).

InspectionCreate.title: InspectionCreate
InspectionCreate.description:
Request body for POST /api/operations/{id}/inspect.

`supersedes_inspection_id` opts into Resolve Conditional Finding
mode (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.5.5 / R5-R2-ISSUE-006): the inspector
is resolving a prior `conditional` inspection on the same
operation.  Frontend derives this from the `?resolves=<id>`
query parameter on the inspection route.  Absent / None means
a normal first-time inspection.

`evidence_refs` entries are structured submissions (build spec
v1.4.2 Decision 1): only `s3_key` is load-bearing — the service
hydrates the full ref metadata from the evidence_confirmations
registry.  Bare-string refs are rejected at the service layer.

InspectionOut.title: InspectionOut
InspectionOut.description:
Inspection event in API responses.

`evidence_refs` echoes the persisted structured refs verbatim.
Legacy rows written before the Decision-1 contract may surface
as bare strings — the read path tolerates that shape; the
Pydantic type here is a permissive list of objects OR strings
so the response validates against every row already in the DB.

InspectionQueueRowOut.title: InspectionQueueRowOut
InspectionQueueRowOut.description:
Single row in the Inspection Queue read-model (UX spec §5.5.5).

Keyed by operation_id — one row per operation with queue-relevant
hold-point state.  The row mixes the operation, its parent WO,
and (for conditional rows) the latest current-cycle conditional
inspection the inspector is being asked to resolve.

Field notes:
- program_id: pulled through the WO join; enables the §3.2 auto-
  switch behavior in the frontend when a cross-program deep-link
  lands on a conditional row.
- state: the server-assigned queue bucket per §5.5.5 (pending /
  conditional / overdue / completed).  The frontend does not
  re-derive this.
- hold_point_status: the §5.4.3 operation-level hold status; kept
  alongside `state` so queue rows carry the same vocabulary the
  operation detail surface uses (prevents drift between queue
  copy and detail page copy).
- is_overdue / overdue_since: null when the op has not crossed
  the program's overdue_threshold_hours.  overdue_since is the
  moment the op became overdue, computed server-side from
  started_at + overdue_threshold_hours — stable across polls so
  "time overdue" can be rendered by the client.
- conditional_inspection_id: present ONLY on state=conditional
  rows.  The frontend passes this as `?resolves=<id>` on the
  Inspection Form link (§5.5.5, R5-R2-ISSUE-006).  Null for all
  other states.
- inspected_at: the timestamp of the inspection that drove the
  row's current hold_point_status (pending → null).

InspectionQueueState.title: InspectionQueueState
InspectionQueueState.description:
Server-derived Inspection Queue bucket (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.5.5).

The queue is a read-model over operations with an inspection hold.
State is derived from (a) current-cycle inspection history and
(b) the overdue-threshold clock on the parent program.  Buckets:

- pending: hold_point_status == pending (no current-cycle inspection).
  These are the rows at the top of an inspector's worklist.
- conditional: hold_point_status == conditionally_satisfied.  Latest
  current-cycle inspection was conditional; post-completion
  resolution is allowed (spec §5.5.5).
- overdue: pending or conditional AND op has been in_progress longer
  than the program's overdue_threshold_hours (spec §5.1).
- completed: hold_point_status == satisfied.  Historical — used by
  qa_manager drill-through and audit review.

InspectionResult.title: InspectionResult
InspectionResult.description: Inspection outcome recorded by the inspector (spec §3.1 InspectionEvent).

IntegrityFailureOut.title: IntegrityFailureOut
IntegrityFailureOut.description:
Single integrity-check failure per UX spec v1.5.1 §6.6.

Mirrors forge.audit.integrity.IntegrityFailure; lives in the
schema layer so the API contract is independent of the internal
dataclass shape.

LaborCreate.title: LaborCreate
LaborCreate.description:
Request body for POST /api/operations/{id}/labor.

`version_assertions` is optional per UX spec §5.4.2 and §6.3.3;
when present, the server validates each asserted version against
the corresponding live entity and returns 409 on any mismatch.

LaborOut.title: LaborOut
LaborOut.description:
Labor entry in API responses.

`execution_cycle` is the parent operation's cycle at the time
this labor row was created (build spec v1.4.2 GC-2).  Clients
can group labor by cycle to report remediation hours
separately from original-cycle hours.

LaborUpdate.title: LaborUpdate
LaborUpdate.description:
Request body for PATCH /api/labor-entries/{id}.

`version` is optional so an If-Match header can satisfy the
§6.3.1 assertion instead (route reconciles via
resolve_version_assertion).  Spec: labor:update_own allows
updating own entries, labor:update_any allows updating any
entry.

LaborVersionAssertions.title: LaborVersionAssertions
LaborVersionAssertions.description:
Optional §6.3.3 composite version assertions for labor handoff.

UX spec v1.5.1 §5.4.2 names three assertable entities on the
canonical labor-start endpoint:

  - target_operation:   the operation being handed off TO
                        (the op_id in the URL).
  - active_labor_entry: the user's currently-active labor entry
                        that will be implicitly stopped.
  - active_operation:   the operation that active labor entry
                        is on (the op being handed off FROM).

Each field is optional — clients submit only the versions they
observed.  A missing field means "no assertion."  When absent,
the server runs its current default behavior; when present,
every supplied assertion is checked and a single stale entry
triggers a composite 409.

MaterialAccept.title: MaterialAccept
MaterialAccept.description:
Request body for PATCH /api/material-certs/{id}/accept.

Spec §5.15 requires version on state transitions.  SOD-003 enforced
in service.

MaterialConsume.title: MaterialConsume
MaterialConsume.description:
Request body for POST /api/material-certs/{id}/consume.

operation_id is required — consumption is always against a specific
operation (spec §3.1 MaterialConsumption model).  quantity must be
positive; the atomic balance check is in the service layer.

version is the cert's optimistic-lock version (spec §5.15).  We
version the cert, not the consumption, because consume is the
write that mutates cert.quantity_remaining — two concurrent consumes
race on the cert row, and the version check pairs with SELECT FOR
UPDATE to turn a lost-update conflict into a clean 409 instead of
silently over-drawing.

MaterialReceive.title: MaterialReceive
MaterialReceive.description:
Request body for POST /api/material-certs (receive a new lot).

received_by_id is taken from the auth context server-side and is
not accepted from the client — SOD-003 anchor.

NCRClose.title: NCRClose
NCRClose.description:
Request body for POST /api/ncrs/{id}/close (dispositioned → closed).

Spec §5.15: version is required on state-transition endpoints.
Optional root_cause may be recorded at closure for the audit trail.

NCRCreate.title: NCRCreate
NCRCreate.description:
Request body for POST /api/ncrs (creates in `open`).

initiated_by_id is taken from the auth context server-side and is
not accepted from the client — that is the SOD-002 anchor.

NCRDisposition.title: NCRDisposition
NCRDisposition.description:
Request body for PATCH /api/ncrs/{id}/disposition (open → dispositioned).

Spec §5.15: version is required.  SOD-002 (initiator independence)
is enforced in the service layer, not here.

`remediation_work_order_id` is required at disposition time when
the disposition is rework/repair and the NCR's parent WO is
already `closed` (build spec v1.4.2 GC-2).  In the common case
(parent WO not closed) the field is ignored — the parent WO is
reactivated in place.

`version_assertions` is optional per UX spec §6.3.3 composite-
mutation concurrency.  When supplied, the service layer
validates each named entity's version against the live row
BEFORE any mutation, raising a single composite 409 listing
every mismatch.  When absent, only the legacy NCR-scoped
`version` field is checked — existing clients remain compatible.

NCRDispositionVersionAssertions.title: NCRDispositionVersionAssertions
NCRDispositionVersionAssertions.description:
UX spec v1.5.1 §6.3.3 composite version assertions for NCR disposition.

NCR disposition is a composite mutation — a single call can
mutate the NCR (new status + disposition), reopen the linked
operation (complete → in_progress, cycle++), and reactivate the
parent work order (complete → in_progress).  Each entity gets
its own optional assertion; a single stale version triggers a
§6.3.3 composite 409 listing every mismatched entity in one
response.

  - ncr:          the NCR being dispositioned.
  - operation:    the linked operation that will reopen.
  - work_order:   the parent WO that will reactivate.

All fields are optional — callers submit only the versions they
observed.  A missing field means "no assertion"; the server
proceeds without checking that entity's version beyond the
legacy single-NCR `version` field still validated below.  For
rework/repair with side effects, front-ends that care about
exact-match semantics SHOULD supply all three.

NCROut.title: NCROut
NCROut.description:
NCR projected for API responses.

`evidence_refs` echoes the persisted structured refs.  Legacy
rows may carry bare-string entries — the read path tolerates
that shape until the cleanup job hydrates all rows.

NCRPatch.title: NCRPatch
NCRPatch.description:
Request body for PATCH /api/ncrs/{id} (build spec v1.4.2 Decision 1).

This slice restricts the patch surface to evidence refs — the
broader NCR-edit redesign is deliberately out of scope.
`evidence_refs` entries carry only s3_key; the service hydrates
structured metadata from the evidence_confirmations registry.
Replace semantics: the submitted list becomes the full
canonical list on success.

NCRStatus.title: NCRStatus
NCRStatus.description:
NCR lifecycle: open → dispositioned → closed, with voided (spec §3.1).

voided is only valid from the open state.

OpStatus.title: OpStatus
OpStatus.description:
Operation lifecycle status (spec §4.3).

Transitions: pending → in_progress → complete, with hold and rework
branches.  execution_cycle increments on rework → in_progress.

OperationCreate.title: OperationCreate
OperationCreate.description: Request body for POST /api/work-orders/{id}/operations (draft WO only).

OperationDetailOut.title: OperationDetailOut
OperationDetailOut.description:
Enriched operation detail response (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.4.8).

Used by both the engineer Operation Detail page (§5.4.11) and the
operator Operation Execution SSE reconnect contract (§6.5.2 — the
client refetches this endpoint as the authoritative reconciliation
surface on every reconnect, regardless of any best-effort SSE
replay).

`program_id` is required so the client auto-switch behavior
(§3.2 / §6.7.4) can identify the entity's owning program after a
deep-link fetch where the caller's currently-selected program may
differ from the entity's program.

`hold_point_status` is server-derived (spec §5.4.3 explicitly
forbids client-side traversal of inspection history).  See the
KNOWN CONTRACT MISMATCH note in
forge.services.operation_service._derive_hold_point_status — the
`conditionally_satisfied` value is exposed per spec but COMP-001
completion enforcement still requires `accept`.

`predecessor_summaries` carries enough data for the disabled
[Start Timer] tooltip in one round-trip.  When the WO has any
explicit predecessor edges, each op's summary is sourced from
those edges (roots have empty `predecessors`); otherwise the
summary falls back to default-sequential by `sequence`.

`stop_requests` contains only PENDING rows — fulfilled / expired
entries live in the audit trail (§6.6).

OperationReorder.title: OperationReorder
OperationReorder.description:
Request body for POST /api/work-orders/{id}/operations/reorder.

version is the WO's version for optimistic locking — the WO
is the parent entity being logically mutated by reordering.

OperationStartRequest.title: OperationStartRequest
OperationStartRequest.description: Start request includes role and shift for the labor entry.

OperationTransition.title: OperationTransition
OperationTransition.description: Request body for operation state-transition endpoints.

OperationUpdate.title: OperationUpdate

PartUpdate.title: PartUpdate
PartUpdate.description:
Request body for PATCH /api/parts/{id}.

Spec §5.15: version required on mutations.  status transitions
are validated against VALID_PART_TRANSITIONS in the service.

`reason_ncr_id` is required when `status == scrapped` per UX spec
v1.5.1 §5.6.5 (Part Scrap Transition — the QA-closure flow that
posts {status: "scrapped", reason_ncr_id: <ncr_id>}).  Service
layer enforces the "required-for-scrap" rule plus NCR scope and
relationship checks.

PredecessorChange.title: PredecessorChange
PredecessorChange.description:
One add / remove edit to the predecessor graph.

`action="add"` inserts a new edge (operation_id depends on
predecessor_id); `action="remove"` deletes an existing edge.
The service applies every change to a working copy before
validating, so the order of changes within a request does not
matter — the final edge set is what gets validated.

Action is a Literal rather than an Enum so the OpenAPI client
renders it as a string union without a separate enum type —
matches the wire-example JSON in UX spec §5.4.6.

PredecessorSummary.title: PredecessorSummary
PredecessorSummary.description:
Minimal predecessor data per UX spec v1.5.1 §5.4.8.

Drives the disabled [Start Timer] tooltip ("Waiting for: Op N —
description (status)") without requiring the client to fetch each
predecessor in a follow-up call.  Field set is intentionally
minimal so the response stays small for operations with many
predecessors.

`sequence_number` is the spec wire name; the underlying model
column is named `sequence`.  The service layer maps that on
construction so this schema stays spec-accurate without
renaming the database column.

ProgramCreate.title: ProgramCreate
ProgramCreate.description:
Request body for POST /api/admin/programs.

Feature flags are optional on create and fall back to the model /
DB defaults (schedule_enabled=true, oracle_access=false,
overdue_threshold_hours=24).  This matches the rollout intent: a
new program ships with schedule visible, chat opted out, and the
standard 24-hour overdue threshold.

ProgramListItemOut.title: ProgramListItemOut
ProgramListItemOut.description:
Program list item — extends ProgramOut with member_count.

Admin Programs page (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.10) renders a list with
"member count" alongside flags.  Computing the count once per row
in the list service avoids N+1 follow-up queries when the admin
has many programs.  The detail GET returns the lighter ProgramOut
because the detail page does not display the count.

ProgramOut.title: ProgramOut
ProgramOut.description:
Program summary for access-scoping display (build spec §5.0.3).

Feature flags are exposed alongside identity fields because the
frontend consumes them on every render path (UX spec v1.5.1 §1.4
drives navigation visibility off schedule_enabled and oracle_access;
§5.1 derives the dashboard overdue rule off overdue_threshold_hours).
Embedding them in the standard Program payload removes a second
round-trip and keeps the wire shape identical wherever a Program
is returned (admin programs CRUD, user.program_memberships, etc.).

`version` is exposed because admin program updates use the standard
optimistic-locking contract (§6.3) — clients must echo the version
they observed on the next PATCH so a concurrent edit by another
admin produces a 409 instead of silently overwriting.

ProgramUpdate.title: ProgramUpdate
ProgramUpdate.description:
Request body for PATCH /api/admin/programs/{id}.

All mutable fields are optional — admin can toggle a single flag
without re-sending the whole record.  None means "leave unchanged"
at the service layer (model_dump(exclude_unset=True) is the
canonical pattern in admin_service).

`version` is OPTIONAL on the wire: UX spec §6.3.1 permits either
body-version OR an If-Match header.  The route reconciles via
`resolve_version_assertion` and rejects missing-both with 400.
Admin updates are typically composite (name + flags in one
request) so body-version is still the ergonomic default, but
tooling that already sets If-Match globally works without
duplicating the assertion.

RoleOut.title: RoleOut
RoleOut.description: Role with permission array for admin and auth display (spec §5.0.2).

ScheduleTransition.title: ScheduleTransition
ScheduleTransition.description: Request body for state-transition POST endpoints (baseline).

SignOffAction.title: SignOffAction
SignOffAction.description: Role-based sign-off decision on an operation (spec §3.1 SignOffEvent).

StopRequestActor.title: StopRequestActor
StopRequestActor.description:
Nested `requested_by` object on StopRequestOut.

Pre-resolves display_name so the frontend does not need a
follow-up /api/users/{id} round trip to render the engineer's
amber-indicator tooltip.

StopRequestIn.title: StopRequestIn
StopRequestIn.description:
Request body for POST /api/labor-entries/{id}/stop-request.

`labor_entry_version` is optional when an If-Match header is
supplied; route reconciles.

StopRequestOut.title: StopRequestOut
StopRequestOut.description:
Stop-request entity in API responses (UX spec §5.4.9).

Wire-stable across the POST /stop-request success (201) and the
operation-detail read embed (§5.4.8 stop_requests array).  Only
`pending` rows appear in the default operation-detail response —
fulfilled and expired live in the audit trail — but the schema
carries the full lifecycle enum so a future admin read surface
can return history without a schema fork.

StopRequestStatus.title: StopRequestStatus
StopRequestStatus.description:
Stop-request lifecycle (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.4.9 Stop-Request Lifecycle).

- pending: request created; awaiting engineer action.
- fulfilled: the associated labor entry was force-stopped by an
  engineer via POST /api/labor-entries/{id}/force-stop.
- expired: the labor entry was stopped by another mechanism
  (operator self-stop, hold-cascade, session timeout) before
  any engineer acted on the request.

Transitions from `pending` are ALWAYS server-managed; the spec
leaves no client-driven path for fulfilled/expired.

StopRequestSummary.title: StopRequestSummary
StopRequestSummary.description:
Pending stop-request summary per UX spec v1.5.1 §5.4.8 / §5.4.9.

The operation-detail response serializes only `pending` rows
here.  Fulfilled and expired entries live in the audit trail
(§6.6) and are not returned on this read surface.

`requested_by` is a nested object (user_id + display_name) so
the engineer's Operation Detail view can render the amber
indicator + operator attribution without a follow-up
/api/users/{id} round trip.  The shape mirrors
forge.schemas.stop_request.StopRequestActor — the inline dict
typing here avoids a cross-schema import on the read path.

StoppedLaborEntryOut.title: StoppedLaborEntryOut
StoppedLaborEntryOut.description:
Single entry in WorkOrderHoldOut.stopped_labor_entries
(UX spec v1.5.1 §5.3 Hold Cascading + §6.5.2 SSE payload
requirements).

Intentionally minimal: the frontend stop-work banner (§5.3) needs
exactly `entry_id` / `operation_id` / `user_id` to decide whether
the current user's own timer was force-stopped.  Timestamps are
available via a follow-up read if needed.

TraceLinkType.title: TraceLinkType
TraceLinkType.description: Relationship types between traced entities (spec §3.1 TraceabilityLink).

TraceSourceType.title: TraceSourceType
TraceSourceType.description: Entity types that can participate in traceability links (spec §3.1).

TraceabilityOut.title: TraceabilityOut
TraceabilityOut.description:
Full traceability chain for a part (spec §5.7).

`assembly_chain` walks parent_assembly_id upward (current → parent →
grandparent).  `child_parts` lists any direct children (parts whose
parent_assembly_id is this part).  `links` is all TraceabilityLink
rows where this part appears as either source or target.

UserOut.title: UserOut
UserOut.description:
User detail with eagerly-embedded roles and program memberships.

Roles and programs are embedded (not linked) because admin callers
need the full permission set and access scope in a single response
to render the user management UI without follow-up queries.

is_system_actor is exposed so the admin UI can render it as
read-only and prevent mutation attempts on the SYSTEM account
(spec §3.1 — system actor records are immutable).

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description:
Fields updatable via PATCH /api/admin/users/{id}.

Only display_name and active are mutable via admin CRUD.
email and cognito_sub are identity fields managed by Cognito.
is_system_actor is immutable after provisioning (spec §3.1).
Role and program assignments use dedicated endpoints.

WOStatus.title: WOStatus
WOStatus.description:
Work order lifecycle status (spec §4.3).

Transitions: draft → released → in_progress → complete → closed,
with hold branching from released or in_progress.

WhatIfLinkOverride.title: WhatIfLinkOverride
WhatIfLinkOverride.description: Hypothetical lag_hours for an existing schedule link.

WhatIfOperationOverride.title: WhatIfOperationOverride
WhatIfOperationOverride.description: Hypothetical estimated_hours for an existing operation.

WhatIfOut.title: WhatIfOut
WhatIfOut.description:
Response body for POST /api/schedules/{id}/what-if.

delta_hours is positive when the what-if finishes later than the
current forecast.  cycle_detected indicates the hypothetical
graph contained a cycle — in that case, the new forecast fields
are copies of the current forecast and critical_path_changed is
False (no comparison was possible).

WhatIfRequest.title: WhatIfRequest
WhatIfRequest.description:
Request body for POST /api/schedules/{id}/what-if.

All fields are optional; the service layer applies only the
overrides provided and leaves the rest of the schedule at its
current values.  The request never mutates persisted state
(spec §8.3).

WorkOrderCreate.title: WorkOrderCreate
WorkOrderCreate.description: Request body for POST /api/work-orders (creates in draft).

WorkOrderDetailOut.title: WorkOrderDetailOut
WorkOrderDetailOut.description:
Detail response for GET /api/work-orders/{id} (Build Spec §5.1).

Why this shape: Build Spec §5.1 routes table documents the detail
endpoint as "Get work order detail with operations", and §3.1
WorkOrder class carries ``operations: list[Operation]`` in its
relationships.  The list endpoint continues to return the lighter
``WorkOrderOut`` (no operations) so paginated responses stay small.
The detail endpoint returns this subtype so the frontend work-order
detail page (UX spec §5.3) can render the Operations tab without a
second round trip.

Operations are ordered by ``sequence`` ascending — matches the
UX spec's operations table column order and avoids the client
having to re-sort a paginated list.

WorkOrderHoldIn.title: WorkOrderHoldIn
WorkOrderHoldIn.description:
Request body for POST /api/work-orders/{id}/hold (UX spec v1.5.1
§5.3 Hold Cascading).

`version` is optional to support the §6.3.1 If-Match alternative
(route-level `resolve_version_assertion` enforces exactly-one-of
body.version or If-Match is present).  `force_stop_labor`
defaults to False (administrative hold).  When True, the server
atomically stops all active labor entries on child operations
and emits one `labor.stopped_by_hold` audit event per stopped
entry.  `reason` is currently nullable — the spec mentions a
hold reason but the frozen contract (§5.3 Hold Cascading
subsection) only binds it as future SSE payload data, so the
field is accepted and stored in the audit before_state but not
required.

WorkOrderHoldOut.title: WorkOrderHoldOut
WorkOrderHoldOut.description:
Response for POST /api/work-orders/{id}/hold.

Returns the post-hold WorkOrder plus the cascade metadata needed
for the §5.3 stop-work banner and the §6.5.2 SSE payload.  When
`force_stop_labor` is False, `stopped_labor_entries` is always an
empty list — wire-stable so the client does not have to branch.

WorkOrderOut.title: WorkOrderOut
WorkOrderOut.description:
Work order in API responses.

`has_graph_issue` (UX spec v1.5.1 §5.4.6) ships on every WO
response — list, detail, and every state-transition response —
so the frontend never has to compose a separate fetch to render
the [Fix Graph] / [Report Graph Issue] buttons.  The field is
written by the graph validator at release + Fix Graph + Report
Graph Issue; reads treat it as authoritative.

WorkOrderStatusCounts.title: WorkOrderStatusCounts
WorkOrderStatusCounts.description:
Per-status work-order totals for the Build Status card.

Keys mirror forge.models.enums.WOStatus exactly so consumers that
enumerate the enum can use the values directly without a mapping
layer.  Zero is a valid count — the tile still renders with a
zero bar rather than hiding, giving a consistent footprint.

WorkOrderTransition.title: WorkOrderTransition
WorkOrderTransition.description:
Request body for state-transition POST endpoints.

Same contract as WorkOrderUpdate: body-version is optional so
an If-Match header alone satisfies §6.3.1.

WorkOrderUpdate.title: WorkOrderUpdate
WorkOrderUpdate.description:
Request body for PATCH /api/work-orders/{id} (draft only).

Spec §6.3.1 allows either `version` in the body OR an
`If-Match` header for optimistic locking.  Making `version`
optional here keeps the body contract lenient — the route
resolves the effective expected version via
forge.api.concurrency.effective_expected_version and rejects
missing-both with 400 MISSING_VERSION, mismatched-both with
409 VERSION_CONFLICT.  Callers still using body-only continue
unchanged.
